header.title: How to Replace a Chest Freezer Compressor
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to replace the compressor in a chest freezer. It covers removing the old compressor, installing the new one, and completing the necessary finishing steps to restore freezer functionality.

steps.description: This step involves disconnecting and removing the old compressor from the freezer.
actions: Make sure the freezer is unplugged.
Remove the cover of the area where the compressor is located.
Remove the clip cover using long-nose pliers.
Remove the cover overload using your hand.
Take out the clip overload using long nose pliers.
Remove the common, running, and starting terminal connections individually using your hands.
Free the compressor from the remaining freon by breaking the charging tube using long nose pliers.
Disconnect the suction and discharge tubes from the compressor using a torch with Mapp gas.
Detach the compressor by removing the bolts and nuts attached to the compressor base.

steps.description: This step details the installation of a new compressor, including connecting tubes, installing electrical components, and evacuating/charging the system with freon.
actions: Attach the new compressor to the compressor base using the bolts and nuts.
Use a torch with Mapp gas and the silver rod to connect the suction and discharge tubes.
Install a new charging tube.
Install a clip overload.
Attach the running and starting terminal using the relay.
Thread the neutral pressure gauge (NPG) to the vacuum pump using the manifold.
Take out existing air and any tiny particles from the tubing and the compressor.
Plug in the vacuum pump.
Let the vacuum pump work for 30 minutes.
Check if compressor and tubing are totally voided of air.
Close the LPG knob.
Turn off the vacuum pump.
Transfer the NPG from the vacuum pump to the freon tank.
Open the freon tank.
Loosen the NPG valve to release existing air off the hose.
Start charging freon to the compressor based on the suggested PSI.
Plug in the chest freezer while waiting for the freon to regulate.

steps.description: This step involves closing the freon tank, removing the hose, and installing the compressor.
actions: Close the freon tank
Remove the hose connected to it
Slide in the compressor to its proper place
